Parse a saved Google Scholar results page

Source: R/scholar.R
scholar_parse_html.Rd

Reads a Google Scholar search-results page that you saved from your browser and pulls out what the results list shows for each hit: title, authors, venue, year, publisher, link, snippet, citation count and number of versions. It parses the page's HTML/XML with the xml2 package; it does **not** contact Google Scholar, which blocks automated requests and whose terms do not allow them.

Usage

scholar_parse_html(input, recursive = FALSE)

Arguments

input

One or more paths to saved `.html` files, **a folder** (every `.html` / `.htm` file in it is read), or a string of HTML text. Results from several pages are combined.

recursive

If `input` is a folder, also read files in its subfolders.

Value

A data frame with one row per result: `source_file` (the file it came from), `title`, `authors` (as shown, with initials), `author_list` (a list column of names), `authors_truncated`, `venue`, `venue_truncated`, `year`, `publisher`, `url`, `snippet`, `cited_by`, `versions` and `cid` (Scholar's internal id for the result).

Details

To save a page in Chrome or Safari: open the results, then File > Save Page As (choose "Webpage, HTML Only" or "Page Source"). Save each results page you want as its own file.

The results list shortens long author lists and venue names with "...", and does not show volume, pages or DOI. Entries affected are flagged in `authors_truncated` and `venue_truncated`. For complete records, use Scholar's **Cite > BibTeX** (or **My library > Export**) instead.

Examples

page <- '<div class="gs_r" data-cid="x1"><div class="gs_ri">
  <h3 class="gs_rt"><a href="https://example.org/a">Retention and <b>advising</b></a></h3>
  <div class="gs_a">A Smith, B Jones - Journal of Examples, 2019 - Example Press</div>
  <div class="gs_fl"><a>Cite</a> <a>Cited by 12</a></div></div></div>'
scholar_parse_html(page)
#>   source_file                  title                 authors  author_list
#> 1        <NA> Retention and advising Smith, A. and Jones, B. Smith, A....
#>   authors_truncated               venue venue_truncated year     publisher
#> 1             FALSE Journal of Examples           FALSE 2019 Example Press
#>                     url snippet cited_by versions cid
#> 1 https://example.org/a    <NA>       12       NA  x1
